newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moslem rebels slaughter 30 in Algeria - official.
newsitem.headline: Moslem rebels slaughter 30 in Algeria - official.

text.p: Moslem guerrillas killed 30 people overnight in Chebli village, 50 km (30 miles) south of the Algerian capital, Algiers, said the Algerian security forces in a statement on Monday.

The statement, released by the official Algerian news agency APS, said the 30 people were "assassinated in a cowardly way by a terrorist gang", the official term used for rebels committing murders by cutting throats.
The four-line statement gave no details on the Chebli's massacre, the second mass killing in three days. The latest massacre brought to about 180 the number of people killed during the past week.
In a similar raid on Friday night, Moslem rebels slaughtered 22 villagers in the neighbouring village of Menaa.
In the worst attack in five years of violence in Algeria, Moslem guerrillas exterminated all the 52 inhabitants of a village in Medea province, 70 km (45 miles) south of Algiers, last week.

Algerian commentators see the renewed killings as a common pattern by the guerrillas to step up violence ahead of political events to embarrass the authorities in their drive to end violence without the participation of radical Islamists.

Algeria is gearing up for June 5 legislative elections in which more than 30 political parties will take part, including the main secular opposition Socialist Forces Front group which boycotted earlier elections.
The outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) called on Algerians to boycott the legislative elections saying they would be neither free nor fair.
Algeria has been without an elected parliament since January 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which FIS had taken a commanding lead.
About 60,000 people have died in the North African country's five-year-old violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces.
